items.summary: A zkSNARK prototype proves a response came from the claimed model without revealing its weights, demonstrated on Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE, 4-bit): 110 tokens per second of proving on one H100, about 19 MB per 1,024-token request, at 70–95x vLLM's GPU cost, with client verification in roughly 17 seconds. It proves an integer model under greedy decoding only, caps context at 1,024 tokens and hides weights but not architecture; code is Apache-2.0 and ships with Lean proofs.
items.title: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, cryptographic proof that a 400B model served a reply

items.summary: Two engineers had the model produce the enclosure, circuit board and firmware for a device that interacts with Codex, with a contract manufacturer building a small batch of prototypes in under a month; several revisions were needed where Astra missed manufacturing constraints. OpenAI also reports BenchCAD 2.0, a benchmark for reconstructing 3D parts and assemblies on which an internal model averages 0.875, and 23-fold growth in internal hardware-team usage since February.
items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a working Codex companion device in under a week

items.summary: An autonomous search over both algorithms and systems raises single-request speedup over autoregressive decoding from a stock 4.46x to 10.87x, and batched speedup from 1.94x to 3.93x, across four target models, three drafters, two GPU platforms and five benchmarks, with no training and no quality loss. It turns the compute accounting of [[2026-11-03#2|the predict-gate-execute analysis]] into an automatically tuned system.
items.title: SpecPilot discovers speculative-decoding algorithms, lifting speedup from 4.46x to 10.87x

items.summary: A pretrained video diffusion model is repurposed as a universal latent action learner, compressing each latent video frame from 1,200 tokens to 4. The authors report state-of-the-art results among latent action models on LARY-Bench, plus zero-shot cross-embodiment action transfer and cheaper downstream policy learning.
items.title: DreamX turns a video diffusion model into a latent action learner at 300x compression

items.summary: Q3 revenue of $13.4B with data center up 96.9% to $8.55B, a record quarter, and a raised 2027 growth outlook; MI450 Helios racks are in initial operation. Lisa Su said OpenAI chose EPYC Turin CPUs to host its first custom accelerator platforms, and more than 240 platforms are committed to the next-generation EPYC Venice. It prices the same AI build-out cycle as [[2026-11-04#3|the Marvell–Lumentum merger]].
items.title: AMD data center revenue nearly doubles to $8.5B; OpenAI picks EPYC Turin for its own chips

items.summary: A trajectory matrix of 374,401 scored runs over 452 candidate configurations and 25 benchmarks puts per-input oracle routing 5.4 points above the best single candidate. Learned routers recover 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, 2.1 on video generation and 1.1 on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time, and routing raises efficiency 8.82x on average over the reference model.
items.title: Route Anything: per-input oracle routing beats the best fixed model by 5.4 points

items.summary: Harder synthesised versions of AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking drop seven frontier models by up to 38.2 points; training on the generated environments raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6. It applies the task-synthesis route of [[2026-11-02#3|WorkFactory]] to tool environments rather than occupations.
items.title: ToolSpace synthesises tool environments and lifts GLM-5.2 to 56.6, Claude Opus 5 level

items.summary: The system learns a domain from its own experience, storing skills and reflections in a knowledge repository instead of relying on human experts or a stronger teacher: held-out all-pass rate on Harvey's LAB Firm Knowledge rises from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash. It is the research-side counterpart to [[2026-11-04#0|Anthropic's recursive self-improvement warning to the SEC]] and to [[2026-11-01#6|Xiaomi's A-RSI]].
items.title: Alibaba's Recursa self-improves into new domains with no teacher: 30% to 55% on legal

items.summary: A 31-page technical report argues later tokens cost up to 7x more than earlier ones on frontier open-weight models, that frequent context compaction costs little to no task accuracy on long-horizon and long-input work, and that performance does not collapse on long-horizon SWE tasks even at one action per context. It proposes semantic state space models as the alternative to extending windows.
items.title: "You don't need long context": compaction matches long-context runs on SWE tasks

lead: Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve, a prototype that cryptographically proves a response came from the model a provider claims to have used, running at 110 tokens per second on a single H100 against a 400B-parameter model.
